chapters.situation: The Ahmedabad mill strike is underway. Meanwhile the Ashram at Kochrab has grown to over forty people.
chapters.summary: Plague breaks out in Kochrab village, and Gandhi decides to move. Punjabhai Hirachand finds land on the Sabarmati river near the Central Jail, which Gandhi likes because jail is a satyagrahi's natural lot. They buy it within eight days and live in tents among snakes. The rule of not killing snakes has held at Phoenix, Tolstoy Farm and Sabarmati with no deaths from snakebite in 25 years, which Gandhi credits to God. The foundations of a weaving shed are laid.

updates.gandhi: Moves the Ashram to the Sabarmati riverbank beside the Central Jail.
updates.maganlal: Carries out the move to the new site.
updates.ashram: Moves from plague-hit Kochrab to the banks of the Sabarmati. Over forty people live in tents with a tin kitchen. Weaving is its main work, as spinning is not yet possible.
updates.sabarmati: The Ashram's permanent home from 1917, near the Central Jail.
updates.ahimsa: No snakes are killed at Phoenix, Tolstoy Farm or Sabarmati, and there is no death from snakebite in 25 years.

status.ashram: At Sabarmati, near the Central Jail

chapters.situation: Ahmedabad's mill-hands have been on strike for two weeks under Gandhi's four conditions, and their resolve is weakening.
chapters.summary: As the strikers grow despondent and threatening toward strikebreakers, Gandhi declares he will fast until they rally or a settlement is reached. The workers, shaken, recommit, and carry sand for the Ashram's weaving school to earn wages, led by Anasuyabehn with a basket on her head. Gandhi admits the fast unfairly pressures his friends the mill-owners, Ambalal and Sarladevi. After three days the owners agree to arbitration by Anandshankar Dhruva, ending the 21-day strike. Hungry beggars spoil the celebratory sweet distribution.

updates.gandhi: Fasts for the first time in India for a public cause. Admits the fast unfairly pressured the mill-owners.
updates.anasuyabai: Weeps at the fast announcement and leads the strikers carrying sand.
updates.ambalal: Gandhi admires his will and sincerity and is pained by the strain his fast puts on him. He agrees to arbitration.
updates.vallabhbhai: Tries to find the strikers municipal work.
updates.maganlal: Suggests employing the strikers to carry sand for the weaving school.
updates.millstrike: Settled after 21 days through arbitration, after three days of Gandhi's fast.
updates.satyagraha: A satyagrahi may not fast to coerce an opponent, only for his own side's lapse.
updates.diet: Gandhi breaks his fast after three days when the strike is settled.

chapters.situation: The Ahmedabad strike has just ended. Kheda's peasants, the Patidars, face near-famine after their crops failed, but the government insists on collecting land revenue.
chapters.summary: Under the revenue rules, a crop of four annas or less (a quarter of normal) entitles peasants to suspension of the assessment. The peasants say theirs was below that; the government says it was above, and refuses arbitration. After petitions fail, Gandhi, as president of the Gujarat Sabha, advises satyagraha. Vallabhbhai Patel gives up his thriving legal practice for good to join. The pledge: refuse to pay, accept forfeiture of land, and let the better-off withhold payment to protect the poor.

updates.gandhi: Launches the Kheda satyagraha against land revenue collection.
updates.vallabhbhai: Suspends his legal practice to join the Kheda fight and never resumes it.
updates.thakkar: Investigated and reported on the Kheda situation.
updates.shankarlalparikh: Raised the Kheda cause early; later writes its history.
updates.anasuyabai: One of Gandhi's principal comrades in Kheda.
updates.desai: One of Gandhi's principal comrades in Kheda.
updates.shankarlal: One of Gandhi's principal comrades in Kheda.
updates.kheda: Headquarters at the Nadiad Anathashram. The pledge is not to pay revenue and to let land be forfeited if necessary.
updates.satyagraha: Satyagraha against land revenue, launched after all petitions failed.

status.vallabhbhai: Left the bar to work full-time with Gandhi

chapters.situation: The Kheda peasants have pledged not to pay land revenue, and the campaign is reported daily in the press.
chapters.summary: Gujaratis send more money than needed, though satyagraha needs money least of all. Gandhi tours villages teaching that officials are servants of the people, and finds civility toward opponents the hardest lesson. The government seizes cattle, movable property and standing crops, and some peasants pay. When Shankarlal Parikh's tenant pays, Parikh gives the land to charity. Gandhi advises removing a wrongly seized onion crop, and Mohanlal Pandya and others are jailed, earning Pandya the title 'onion thief'.

updates.gandhi: Teaches peasants fearlessness and civility. Advises removing a wrongly attached onion crop.
updates.mohanlalpandya: Removes the attached onion crop, is jailed, and is honoured as the 'dungli chor' (onion thief).
updates.shankarlalparikh: Gives away the land on which his tenant paid the assessment.
updates.kheda: The government seizes cattle, goods and crops. Some peasants give in and others hold firm.
updates.satyagraha: 'Civility is the most difficult part of satyagraha': it means inborn gentleness and a desire to do good to the opponent.
updates.jail: 'When the fear of jail disappears, repression puts heart into the people.'
updates.civildisobedience: Removing the onion crop is a lesson in courting jail.

chapters.situation: The Kheda peasants have endured seizures and jailings, and are tiring after months of resistance.
chapters.summary: An official offers that if the well-to-do Patidars pay, the poor will get suspension, and the Collector confirms the order applies district-wide. Since this was the pledge's aim, Gandhi accepts. But hardly any poor peasants benefit, and the ending lacks grace, so it leaves Gandhi unhappy. Still, Kheda begins Gujarat's peasant awakening: educated workers learn to identify with peasants, Vallabhbhai finds himself, and satyagraha takes root in Gujarat's soil.

updates.gandhi: Accepts a compromise ending to Kheda but is dissatisfied with how gracelessly it ends.
updates.vallabhbhai: 'Found himself' in the Kheda campaign, the start of his leadership.
updates.besant: Her Home Rule agitation had touched the peasants first.
updates.kheda: Suspension for the poor is granted on paper but barely applied. It is still the beginning of the Gujarat peasants' political education.
updates.satyagraha: A worthy ending leaves satyagrahis stronger than at the start. Kheda didn't quite manage this, but satyagraha took root in Gujarat.

chapters.situation: The Kheda satyagraha has just ended. World War I is in crisis, and the Viceroy invites Indian leaders to a war conference in Delhi.
chapters.summary: Gandhi objects that the jailed Ali brothers are excluded. He has long believed Hindu–Muslim unity will be the hardest test of his ahimsa, and has been seeking good Muslim friends. He supports the Muslims' Khilafat demands, which the British Prime Minister himself had acknowledged as just. Andrews raises Britain's secret treaties with Italy, but after a long talk with Lord Chelmsford, Gandhi agrees to attend and to put the Muslim case in a letter.

updates.gandhi: Champions the release of the Ali brothers and the Khilafat cause. Agrees to attend the war conference.
updates.alibrothers: In jail; Mahomed Ali writes long letters to Gandhi, who campaigns for their release.
updates.andrews: Questions the morality of joining a war conference given the secret treaties.
updates.rudra: Speaks highly of Hakim Ajmal Khan to Gandhi.
updates.chelmsford: Persuades Gandhi to help the Empire now and raise moral issues after the war.
updates.khilafat: Gandhi backs the Muslim demand, which the British Prime Minister himself had pledged to honour.
updates.islam: Gandhi seeks the friendship of the 'purest and most patriotic' Muslims.
updates.ahimsa: Hindu–Muslim unity is 'the widest field for my experiments in ahimsa'.

chapters.situation: Gandhi has agreed to attend the Viceroy's war conference in Delhi and support its resolutions.
chapters.summary: Gandhi supports the recruiting resolution in one sentence in Hindustani and is pained that this is apparently a first at a viceregal meeting. Rev. Ireland carries his letter to the Viceroy, which promises support while warning that disappointing India's hopes would mean disillusion, and that he will resist tyranny to the utmost. Back in Kheda, Gandhi walks 20 miles a day asking for army recruits. The same peasants who gave carts freely for satyagraha now give nothing and ask how a votary of ahimsa can urge them to take up arms.

updates.gandhi: Speaks in Hindustani at the war conference and tramps through Kheda recruiting soldiers, meeting scepticism.
updates.ireland: Carries Gandhi's letter to the Viceroy, travelling intermediate class.
updates.vallabhbhai: Joins the recruiting effort with misgivings.
updates.tilak: Gandhi regrets his exclusion from the conference.
updates.besant: Gandhi regrets her exclusion from the conference.
updates.alibrothers: Gandhi regrets their exclusion from the conference.
updates.recruiting: Peasants refuse carts and food and ask how a votary of ahimsa can ask them to take up arms. Gandhi argues that serving now could win the repeal of the Arms Act and Home Rule.
updates.loyalty: Gandhi's letter offers unconditional support for the war but warns that 'disappointment of hope means disillusion'.
updates.kheda: The same district turns cold when asked for recruits.

chapters.situation: Gandhi is tramping through Kheda for army recruits, living mostly on groundnut butter and lemons.
chapters.summary: Too much groundnut butter gives Gandhi dysentery. Tempted by a festival meal Kasturba makes, he overeats and the dysentery becomes acute. Refusing all medicine and injections, he grows delirious. Ambalal takes him to his bungalow, but Gandhi insists on going back to the Ashram. News comes that Germany is defeated and recruiting is no longer needed. He refuses meat broth and eggs, listens to the Gita expecting death, and is revived somewhat by the 'Ice Doctor' Kelkar's treatment.

updates.gandhi: Nearly dies of dysentery in 1918, refusing medicine, meat and eggs. Listens to the Gita, expecting the end.
updates.kasturba: Prepares a festival meal that tempts Gandhi into the overeating that worsens his dysentery.
updates.ambalal: Moves Gandhi to his bungalow with his wife and nurses him lovingly.
updates.anasuyabai: Called on the night Gandhi thinks he will die.
updates.kanuga: Diagnoses a nervous breakdown from weakness and pleads with Gandhi to take medicine.
updates.kelkar: The 'Ice Doctor', whose ice treatment gives Gandhi new hope. He urges raw eggs, which Gandhi refuses.
updates.recruiting: Ends with Germany's defeat, to Gandhi's relief.
updates.gita: Read aloud to Gandhi on what he believes is his deathbed.
updates.naturecure: Hydropathy and ice treatment instead of drugs.

chapters.situation: Gandhi is slowly recovering from near-fatal dysentery but cannot rebuild his strength without milk.
chapters.summary: Dr. Dalal says he cannot restore Gandhi without milk. Kasturba points out that his vow covered only cow's and buffalo's milk, and Gandhi gives in and takes goat's milk, keeping the letter of the vow while knowing he has broken its spirit, out of eagerness to fight. Recovering after an operation, he reads the Rowlatt Committee's report recommending repressive powers. With Vallabhbhai, Sarojini Naidu, Horniman and others he drafts a satyagraha pledge at the Ashram and founds the Satyagraha Sabha, with himself as president.

updates.gandhi: Takes goat's milk and still feels remorse about it. Founds the Satyagraha Sabha against the Rowlatt Bills.
updates.kasturba: Suggests goat's milk, leading Gandhi to keep the letter but not the spirit of his vow.
updates.dalal: Insists on milk and operates successfully on Gandhi.
updates.shankarlal: Looks after Gandhi's health and proves a brilliant organizer of the Rowlatt agitation.
updates.vallabhbhai: Visits daily and is among the first signers of the satyagraha pledge.
updates.rowlatt: The committee's recommendations are 'such that no self-respecting people could submit to them'.
updates.satyagrahasabha: Founded in Bombay with Gandhi as president. Its educated members dislike his insistence on truth, ahimsa and Gujarati.
updates.vows: 'The will to live proved stronger than the devotion to truth.' Goat's milk breaks the spirit of his vow.
updates.diet: Goat's milk from 1918–19 onward, against his own principle.

status.gandhi: Taking goat's milk; President, Satyagraha Sabha

chapters.situation: Gandhi has founded the Satyagraha Sabha to resist the Rowlatt Bills, and the government is pressing ahead with them.
chapters.summary: In the Legislative Council Shastri's warning falls on deaf ears; the government is only 'pretending sleep'. Though too weak to speak standing, Gandhi goes to Madras, where Mahadev urges him to cultivate his shy host, C. Rajagopalachari. When the Rowlatt Act is passed, the idea comes to Gandhi in a half-dream: a nationwide hartal, a day of suspended business, fasting and prayer. Set for 6 April 1919, it is observed across all of India.

updates.gandhi: Calls a nationwide hartal for 6 April 1919 after the idea comes to him in a dream. All India responds.
updates.shastri: Gives an impassioned speech warning the government against the Rowlatt Bill.
updates.rajagopalachari: First real meeting. Gandhi's host in Madras, who embraces the hartal idea at once.
updates.desai: Tells Gandhi, 'You should cultivate this man' about Rajagopalachari.
updates.tamil: Gandhi feels a 'special right' over Tamils and Telugus thanks to South Africa.
updates.hartal: 6 April 1919: all India, towns and villages, suspend business for fasting and prayer. 'A most wonderful spectacle.'
updates.satyagraha: Gandhi frames satyagraha as self-purification, to begin with fasting.

chapters.situation: India has observed the nationwide hartal on 6 April against the Rowlatt Act, though Delhi held it early on 30 March.
chapters.summary: In Delhi, Hindus and Muslims unite and Shraddhanand speaks in the Jama Masjid, but police fire on the crowd, and there is trouble in Lahore and Amritsar. In Bombay Gandhi sells his banned books, 'Hind Swaraj' and 'Sarvodaya', as civil disobedience, and buyers pay up to Rs. 50 a copy. Few turn up for the pledges on swadeshi and unity. Heading to the Punjab, he is arrested at Palwal and sent back to Bombay. There a crowd enraged by his arrest is charged by mounted police with lances.

updates.gandhi: Sells banned books, is arrested on his way to the Punjab and returned to Bombay, and witnesses a cavalry charge on the crowd.
updates.shraddhanand: Leads Delhi's hartal and speaks in the Jama Masjid; police fire on the procession. He summons Gandhi.
updates.sarojini: Sells banned books from a car with Gandhi.
updates.desai: Sent to Delhi to keep the people calm after Gandhi's arrest.
updates.anasuyabai: Fetches Gandhi to calm the excited crowd at Pydhuni.
updates.odwyer: His government bans Gandhi from the Punjab.
updates.hartal: A complete success in Bombay. Police fire on hartal crowds in Delhi.
updates.civildisobedience: Banned books are sold openly. The government decides the reprints are not banned at all.
updates.punjab: Gandhi is barred from entering and removed from the train at Palwal.
updates.swadeshi: The pledge is administered carefully to the few who come.
updates.unto: 'Sarvodaya', Gandhi's Gujarati adaptation, is sold as banned literature.
updates.khilafat: Hindus and Muslims unite in the hartal.

status.gandhi: Arrested and released in Bombay, April 1919

chapters.situation: Gandhi's arrest has set off riots. Mounted police have charged a crowd in Bombay, and there is violence elsewhere.
chapters.summary: Commissioner Griffith tells Gandhi the people cannot understand nonviolence; Gandhi insists they are peaceful by nature. In Ahmedabad, rumours of Anasuyabehn's arrest set off mill-worker riots in which a sergeant is killed, and martial law follows. Gandhi holds a meeting at the Ashram and declares a three-day penitential fast, sharing in the workers' guilt. He asks rioters to confess and the government to pardon them; neither does. He suspends satyagraha until the people learn peace.

updates.gandhi: Fasts three days in penance for the Ahmedabad riots and suspends satyagraha.
updates.griffith: Argues that the people will inevitably turn to violence and blames Gandhi.
updates.anasuyabai: Her rumoured arrest triggers the Ahmedabad riots.
updates.ahmedabad: Mill-hands riot, a sergeant is killed, and martial law follows.
updates.satyagraha: Suspended: 'Unless people observe [nonviolence] in thought, word and deed, I cannot offer mass satyagraha.'
updates.ahimsa: Gandhi feels he shares the guilt of those he served.

chapters.situation: After riots in Ahmedabad and elsewhere, Gandhi has suspended satyagraha and fasted in penance.
chapters.summary: At Nadiad, seeing mass arrests in Kheda, Gandhi publicly calls his error a 'Himalayan miscalculation' and is ridiculed for it. A people must first learn willing, intelligent obedience to laws before they earn the right to civilly disobey unjust ones, and he had launched mass civil disobedience too early. He resolves to train a band of pure-hearted volunteers through the Satyagraha Sabha, but finds few interested in the quiet, peaceful side of satyagraha.

updates.gandhi: Publicly confesses a 'Himalayan miscalculation' and starts training satyagrahi volunteers.
updates.himalayan: Calling for mass civil disobedience before people had learned willing obedience to law.
updates.civildisobedience: Only those who have obeyed laws willingly earn the right to disobey unjust ones.
updates.satyagrahasabha: Tries to train volunteers, but recruits dwindle.
updates.truth: See your own mistakes 'with a convex lens' and others' with the reverse.
